turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have about twenty minutes, Hale. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
"An answer today." You asked for this meeting, Hale, and you haven't answered mine. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
Either Owen admits it in writing by Friday at 3 PM or the zero goes on his transcript.

You want a seventeen-year-old to sign a confession by Friday at 3 PM, and you haven't put one document in front of me. I'm writing that down, and the principal will get it tonight. Admit to what, Hale, and under which section of your own procedure?
Those are the only two options. Pick one.

There's a third option, Hale: the zero comes off, and you tell me what you have besides a deadline. Your own procedure says a parent gets a call before any mark goes in, and nobody called me. Pick that one, or I'm going upstairs.
